value.zh: 陳騫
value.en: Chen Qian
value.literal: Chen Qian

value.zh: 瓚字國寶，中書郎，風神高邁，見者皆敬之。
value.en: Zan, whose courtesy name was Guobao, was Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; his bearing was lofty, and all who saw him revered him.
value.literal: Zan, courtesy name Guobao, was Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; his bearing was lofty and transcendent; all who saw him revered him.

value.zh: 特為王綏所重，每從其遊。
value.en: Wang Sui especially esteemed him and constantly accompanied him on outings.
value.literal: Wang Sui especially esteemed him and constantly accompanied him on outings.

value.zh: 綏父戎謂之曰：「國寶初不來，汝數往，何也？」
value.en: Sui's father Rong said to him: "Guobao never comes to you—why do you go to him so often?"
value.literal: Sui's father Rong said to him: "Guobao never comes to you—why do you go to him so often?"

value.zh: 對曰：「國寶雖不知綏，綏自知國寶。」
value.en: He need not notice me," Sui said, "I notice him."
value.literal: [Sui] replied: "Though Guobao does not know Sui, Sui knows Guobao."

value.zh: 楊駿之誅，為亂兵所害。=
value.en: When Yang Jun was executed, Zan was killed by mutinous troops.
value.literal: When Yang Jun was executed, [Zan] was killed by mutinous troops.

value.zh: 初，裴、王二族盛于魏晉之世，時人以為八裴方八王：徽比王祥，楷比王衍，康比王綏，綽比王澄，瓚比王敦，遐比王導，頠比王戎，邈比王玄雲。
value.en: The Pei and Wang houses flourished in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Hui to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuan.
value.literal: At first the Pei and Wang houses flourished side by side in the Wei-Jin age; contemporaries likened eight Peis to eight Wangs: Hui to Wang Xiang, Kai to Wang Yan, Kang to Wang Sui, Chuo to Wang Cheng, Zan to Wang Dun, Xia to Wang Dao, Yi to Wang Rong, and Miao to Wang Xuan.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 張軌
value.en: The subject of this biography is Zhang Gui.
value.literal: Zhang Gui.

value.zh: 晉昌張越，涼州大族，讖言張氏霸涼，自以才力應之。
value.en: Zhang Yue of Jinchang, a powerful Liangzhou lineage, read a prophecy that the Zhangs would dominate the west and believed he was the man.
value.literal: Zhang Yue of Jinchang, a great clan of Liangzhou, believed a prophecy that the Zhang house would rule Liangzhou and thought his own talents matched it.

value.zh: 從隴西內史遷梁州刺史。
value.en: He transferred from Longxi interior administrator to Liangzhou inspector.
value.literal: He moved from interior administrator of Longxi to inspector of Liangzhou.

value.zh: 越志在涼州，遂託病歸河西，陰圖代軌，乃遣兄鎮及曹祛、麹佩移檄廢軌，以軍司杜耽攝州事，使耽表越為刺史。
value.en: His sights were fixed on Liangzhou, so he pretended illness, slipped back to Hexi, and conspired to oust Zhang Gui, circulating a manifesto through his brother Zhang Zhen, Cao Qu, and Qu Pei, installing army supervisor Du Dan and urging the court to name himself inspector.
value.literal: Yue’s ambition lay in Liangzhou; he therefore feigned illness and returned to the west of the river, secretly plotting to supplant Gui. He sent his elder brother Zhen together with Cao Qu and Qu Pei to circulate a proclamation deposing Gui, had Army Supervisor Du Dan act in provincial affairs, and had Dan memorialize recommending Yue as inspector.

value.zh: 軌令曰：「吾在州八年，不能綏靖區域，又值中州兵亂，秦隴倒懸，加以寢患委篤，實思斂跡避賢。
value.en: Zhang Gui issued a notice: “Eight years in office and I have still not quieted the frontier; the heartland is at war and Longyou reels, while my sickness worsens—I would gladly step aside for someone abler.
value.literal: Gui issued an order saying, ‘I have been in this province eight years yet have been unable to pacify the region; moreover the central plain is torn by soldiers, Qin and Long hang upside down, and my illness grows grave—I truly wish to retire and yield the worthy.

value.zh: 但負荷任重，未便輒遂。
value.en: Yet the charge is too heavy to cast off on a whim.
value.literal: But the burden on my shoulders is heavy, and I cannot lightly walk away.

value.zh: 不圖諸人橫興此變，是不明吾心也。
value.en: I never thought you would stir such a revolt; you misread my intentions.
value.literal: I did not expect you gentlemen suddenly to raise this trouble—you do not understand my heart.

value.zh: 吾視去貴州如脫屣耳！」
value.en: To me, leaving your fine province would be as easy as kicking off a slipper!”
value.literal: I regard leaving your noble province as lightly as kicking off a sandal!’

value.zh: 欲遣主簿尉髦奉表詣闕，便速脂轄，將歸老宜陽。
value.en: He meant to send chief clerk Wei Mao to the capital with a memorial, then pack his carriage and retire to Yiyang.
value.literal: He wished to send his chief clerk Wei Mao to present a memorial at the palace gates, then quickly grease the axle hubs and retire to old age in Yiyang.

value.zh: 長史王融、參軍孟暢蹋折鎮檄，排闔諫曰：「晉室多故，人神塗炭，實賴明公撫寧西夏。
value.en: Chief clerk Wang Rong and adjutant Meng Chang shredded Zhang Zhen’s edict, forced their way in, and pleaded: “The Jin court is in crisis; only you can steady the western regions.
value.literal: The chief clerk Wang Rong and adjutant Meng Chang tore up Zhen’s proclamation, burst through the doors, and remonstrated, saying, ‘The house of Jin faces many crises; gods and men are smeared with ashes; we truly depend on you, sir, to soothe the western Xia.

value.zh: 張鎮兄弟敢肆凶逆，宜聲其罪而戮之，不可成其志也。」
value.en: Zhang Zhen’s faction must be denounced and cut down; you cannot let their plot stand.”
value.literal: The brothers Zhang Zhen dare to commit such violence; you should proclaim their crimes and execute them—you must not let them succeed.’

value.zh: 軌嘿然。
value.en: Zhang Gui said nothing.
value.literal: Gui was silent.

value.zh: 融等出而戒嚴。
value.en: When they withdrew, they put the army on full alert.
value.literal: After Rong and the others left, they ordered the troops on alert.

value.zh: 武威太守張琠遣子坦馳詣京，表曰：「魏尚安邊而獲戾，充國盡忠而被譴，皆前史之所譏，今曰之明鑒也。
value.en: Wuwei’s grand administrator Zhang Tian rushed his son Tan to court with a memorial saying, "Wei Shang secured the border yet incurred blame; Zhao Chongguo gave his utmost loyalty yet suffered impeachment—both were mocked by earlier histories and are clear mirrors for today.
value.literal: The grand administrator of Wuwei, Zhang Tian, sent his son Tan posthaste to the capital with a memorial saying, "Wei Shang secured the border yet incurred blame; Zhao Chongguo gave his utmost loyalty yet suffered impeachment—both were mocked by earlier histories and are clear mirrors for today.

value.zh: 順陽之思劉陶，守闕者千人。
value.en: At Shunyang a thousand people besieged the gates for Liu Tao’s sake.
value.literal: In Shunyang a thousand men thronged the palace gates thinking of Liu Tao.

value.zh: 刺史之蒞臣州，若慈母之于赤子，百姓之愛臣軌，若旱苗之得膏雨。
value.en: Your inspector has been a mother to us; the people cherish Zhang Gui as parched shoots welcome rain.
value.literal: When the inspector came to my province it was like a loving mother toward an infant; the people’s love for your servant Gui is like drought-stricken seedlings meeting timely rain.

value.zh: 伏聞信惑流言，當有遷代，民情嗷嗷，如失父母。
value.en: Rumors of his replacement have left the populace wailing like orphans.
value.literal: We have heard that credulous rumors speak of a change of office; the folk wail as if they had lost father and mother.

value.zh: 今戎夷猾夏，不宜騷動一方。」
value.en: With barbarians ravaging the heartland, the west must not be thrown into turmoil.”
value.literal: Now the barbarians are raiding the Xia lands; you ought not to stir up trouble in this region.’

value.zh: 尋以子寔為中督護，率兵討鎮。
value.en: He then named his son Zhang Shi central army supervisor and marched against Zhang Zhen.
value.literal: Shortly thereafter he appointed his son Shi as central army supervisor and led troops against Zhen.

value.zh: 遣鎮外甥太府主簿令狐亞前喻鎮曰：「舅何不審安危，明成敗？
value.en: He sent Zhang Zhen’s nephew Linghu Ya ahead to ask: “Have you weighed the odds, uncle?
value.literal: He sent Zhen’s nephew, chief clerk of the grand treasury Linghu Ya, ahead to lecture Zhen, saying, ‘Uncle, have you not weighed safety against danger and understood success and failure?

value.zh: 主公西河著德，兵馬如雲，此猶烈火已焚，待江漢之水，溺於洪流，望越人之助，其何及哉！
value.en: His lordship’s fame fills the west and his host is like a cloud—waiting for the Yangzi when the blaze has started is futile.
value.literal: Our lord’s virtue is renowned west of the Yellow River, and his soldiers are like clouds—this is like a fire already blazing while you wait for the waters of the Yangzi and Han, or drowning in a flood while you look for help from the Yue—how could that arrive in time!

value.zh: 今數萬之軍已臨近境，今唯全老親，存門戶，輸誠歸官，必保萬全之福。」
value.en: Tens of thousands stand at your gates; save your family by submitting in good faith and you will keep fortune whole."
value.literal: Now several tens of thousands of troops are already at your border; your only course is to preserve your aged kin, save your household, and surrender in good faith to the authorities, and you are sure to win the blessing of perfect safety."

value.zh: 鎮流涕曰：「人誤我也！」
value.en: Zhang Zhen wept, “I was led astray!”
value.literal: Zhen wept and said, ‘Men have misled me!’

value.zh: 乃委罪功曹魯連而斬之，詣寔歸罪。
value.en: He blamed merit clerk Lu Lian, executed him, and went to Zhang Shi to surrender.
value.literal: Thereupon he shifted blame to his merit clerk Lu Lian, beheaded him, and went to Shi to confess guilt.

value.zh: 南討曹祛，走之。
value.en: Zhang Shi took the army south, struck Cao Qu, and sent him fleeing.
value.literal: Zhang Shi marched south against Cao Qu and drove him off.

value.zh: 張坦至自京師，帝優詔勞軌，依模所表，命誅曹祛。
value.en: Zhang Tan’s arrival from Luoyang brought an imperial rescript praising Zhang Gui and, on Sima Mo’s recommendation, commanding Cao Qu’s death.
value.literal: When Tan arrived from the capital, the emperor issued a gracious edict comforting Gui, following Mo’s memorial, and ordered Cao Qu executed.

value.zh: 軌大悅，赦州內殊死已下。
value.en: Zhang Gui rejoiced and declared an amnesty short of capital crimes.
value.literal: Gui was greatly pleased and granted amnesty within the province for all crimes short of capital ones.

value.zh: 命寔率尹員、宋配步騎三萬討祛，別遣從事田迥、王豐率騎八百自姑臧西南出石驢，據長寧。
value.en: He told Zhang Shi to take Yin Yuan, Song Pei, and thirty thousand men against Cao Qu while aides Tian Jiong and Wang Feng led eight hundred horse southwest from Guzang via Stone Mule to seize Changning.
value.literal: He ordered Shi to lead Yin Yuan, Song Pei, and thirty thousand foot and horse against Qu, and separately sent aides Tian Jiong and Wang Feng with eight hundred cavalry southwest from Guzang out through Stone Mule to hold Changning.

value.zh: 怯遣麹晁距戰于黃阪。
value.en: Cao Qu dispatched Qu Chao to hold them at Yellow Slope.
value.literal: Cao Qu sent Qu Chao to oppose them at Yellow Slope.

value.zh: 寔詭道出浩亹，戰於破羌。
value.en: Zhang Shi slipped through Haomen and fought at Poqiang.
value.literal: Shi took a concealed route through Haomen and fought at Poyang.

value.zh: 軌斬祛及牙門田囂。
value.en: Zhang Gui executed Cao Qu and gate captain Tian Xiao.
value.literal: Zhang Gui put Cao Qu and gate guard Tian Ao to death.

value.zh: 二年正月，淮南楊行密舉全吳之眾，精甲五萬，以伐徐州，帝領大軍禦之。
value.en: In the first month of the second year Yang Xingmi of Huainan mustered all Wu with fifty thousand elite armored troops and marched on Xuzhou; the Emperor took the field in force to meet him.
value.literal: In the first month of the second year, Yang Xingmi of Huainan raised all the forces of Wu—fifty thousand picked armored men—to attack Xuzhou; the Emperor led a great army to resist him.

value.zh: 行密聞帝親征，乃收軍而退。
value.en: Hearing the Emperor had come in person, Xingmi pulled his army back.
value.literal: When Xingmi heard the Emperor was campaigning in person, he withdrew his army.

value.zh: 時幽州節度使劉仁恭大舉蕃漢兵號十萬以伐魏，遂攻陷貝州，州民萬餘戶，無少長悉屠之。
value.en: Liu Rengong of Youzhou then raised a mixed tribal and Han host said to number one hundred thousand against Wei, took Beizhou, and slaughtered every soul among its ten thousand-odd households.
value.literal: At that time Liu Rengong, military governor of Youzhou, raised a great force of tribal and Han troops numbering one hundred thousand to attack Wei, captured Beizhou, and of more than ten thousand households in the prefecture, none young or old was spared slaughter.

value.zh: 進攻魏州，魏人來乞師，帝遣硃友倫、張存敬、李思安等先屯于內黃，帝遂親征。
value.en: When Wei sought help against the siege, the Emperor sent Zhu Youlun, Zhang Cunjing, and Li Si'an ahead to Neihuang and followed in person.
value.literal: Advancing to attack Weizhou, the people of Wei came to beg for aid; the Emperor sent Zhu Youlun, Zhang Cunjing, Li Si'an, and others to encamp first at Neihuang, then the Emperor himself campaigned.

value.zh: 三月，與燕軍戰于內黃北，燕軍大敗，殺二萬餘眾，奪馬二千餘匹，擒都將單無敵已下七十餘人。
value.en: In the third month he routed the Yan army north of Neihuang, killing twenty thousand, seizing two thousand horses, and capturing seventy-odd officers down to the famed commander Dan Wudi.
value.literal: In the third month he fought the Yan army north of Neihuang; the Yan army was greatly defeated—more than twenty thousand killed, over two thousand horses captured, and more than seventy commanders from Commander Dan Wudi down were taken.

value.zh: 《通鑒》：單可及，幽州驍將，號單無敵。
value.en: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 notes that Dan Keji was a Youzhou champion known as Dan Wudi—"Peerless Dan."
value.literal: The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Dan Keji was a fierce general of Youzhou, styled Dan Wudi ("Peerless Dan").

value.zh: 是月，葛從周自山東領其部眾，馳以救魏。
value.en: That same month Ge Congzhou raced from Shandong with his division to relieve Wei.
value.literal: That month Ge Congzhou led his troops from Shandong at forced march to relieve Wei.

value.zh: 翼日，乘勝，諸將張存敬以下連破八寨，遂逐燕軍，北至於臨清，壅其殘寇於御河，溺死者甚眾。
value.en: The next day, riding the victory, Zhang Cunjing and the other generals stormed eight camps in a row, drove the Yan army to Linqing, and drowned masses of fugitives in the Imperial Canal.
value.literal: The next day, pressing the victory, the generals from Zhang Cunjing downward broke eight camps in succession, pursued the Yan army north to Linqing, blocked the remnant bandits in the Imperial Canal, and very many drowned.

value.zh: 仁恭奔於滄州。
value.en: Rengong fled to Cangzhou.
value.literal: Rengong fled to Cangzhou.

value.zh: 六月，帝表丁會為潞州節度使，以李罕之疾亟故也。
value.en: In the sixth month the Emperor recommended Ding Hui as governor of Luzhou, Li Hanzhi being gravely ill.
value.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor memorialized to appoint Ding Hui military governor of Luzhou, because Li Hanzhi's illness was acute.

value.zh: 又遣葛從周由固鎮路入於潞州，以援丁會。
value.en: He also sent Ge Congzhou through Guzhen into Luzhou to reinforce Ding Hui.
value.literal: He also sent Ge Congzhou by the Guzhen route into Luzhou to reinforce Ding Hui.

value.zh: 七月壬辰朔，海州陳漢賓擁所部三千奔於淮南。
value.en: On rengchen, the first of the seventh month, Haizhou's Chen Hanbin defected south with three thousand men.
value.literal: On the first day of the seventh month (rengchen), Chen Hanbin of Haizhou led his three thousand troops in flight to Huainan.

value.zh: 戊戌，晉人陷澤州。
value.en: On wuxu the Jin took Zezhou.
value.literal: On wuxu the Jin forces captured Zezhou.

value.zh: 帝遣召葛從周於潞，留賀德倫以守之。
value.en: The Emperor recalled Ge Congzhou from Luzhou and left He Delun to hold the city.
value.literal: The Emperor summoned Ge Congzhou back from Luzhou and left He Delun to defend it.

value.zh: 未幾，德倫為晉人所逼，遂棄潞而歸，由是潞州復為晉人所有。
value.en: Soon pressed by the Jin, Delun abandoned Luzhou; the prefecture was Jin's again.
value.literal: Before long Delun was pressed by the Jin forces, abandoned Luzhou and returned, and thus Luzhou again fell to the Jin.

value.zh: 十一月，陝州都將硃簡殺留後李璠，自稱留後，送款於帝。
value.en: In the eleventh month Shanzhou commander Zhu Jian killed acting governor Li Fan, seized the post, and submitted to the Emperor.
value.literal: In the eleventh month Zhu Jian, garrison commander of Shanzhou, killed the acting governor Li Fan, declared himself acting governor, and submitted allegiance to the Emperor.

value.zh: 三年四月，遣葛從周以兗、鄆、滑、魏之師伐滄州。
value.en: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou with troops from Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei against Cangzhou.
value.literal: In the fourth month of the third year he sent Ge Congzhou with armies from Yan, Yun, Hua, and Wei to attack Cangzhou.

value.zh: 五月庚寅，攻德州，拔之，梟刺史傅公和於城上。
value.en: On gengyin in the fifth month he stormed Dezhou, took it, and exposed Prefect Fu Gonghe's head on the ramparts.
value.literal: On gengyin in the fifth month he attacked Dezhou, captured it, and displayed the head of Prefect Fu Gonghe on the wall.

value.zh: 己亥，進攻浮陽。
value.en: On jihai he pressed the attack on Fuyang.
value.literal: On jihai he advanced to attack Fuyang.

value.zh: 六月，燕帥劉仁恭大舉來援，從周與諸將逆戰于乾寧軍老鴉堤，大破之，殺萬餘眾，俘其將佐馬慎交已下百餘人。
value.en: In the sixth month Liu Rengong marched to relieve the city; Congzhou met him at Laoya Embankment in Qianning Army, crushed his host, killed ten thousand, and took a hundred-odd officers including Ma Shenjiao.
value.literal: In the sixth month the Yan commander Liu Rengong came in force to relieve them; Congzhou and the generals met them in battle at Laoya Embankment in Qianning Army, routed them greatly, killed more than ten thousand, and captured over a hundred of their officers including Ma Shenjiao.

value.zh: 既而以連雨，遂班師。
value.en: Relentless rain then forced a withdrawal.
value.literal: Thereafter because of continuous rain, the army withdrew.

value.zh: 八月，河東遣李進通襲陷洺州，執刺史硃紹宗。
value.en: In the eighth month Hedong's Li Jintong raided and took Mingzhou, capturing Prefect Zhu Shaozong.
value.literal: In the eighth month Hedong sent Li Jintong in a surprise attack that captured Mingzhou and seized Prefect Zhu Shaozong.

value.zh: 帝遣葛從周自鄴縣渡漳水，屯於黃龍鎮，親領中軍涉洺而寨；
value.en: The Emperor sent Ge Congzhou from Yexian across the Zhang to Huanglong Fort while he led the center across the Ming to encamp;
value.literal: The Emperor sent Ge Congzhou from Yexian to cross the Zhang River and encamp at Huanglong Fort; he personally led the central army across the Ming River to make camp;

value.zh: 晉人懼而宵遁，洺州復平。
value.en: the Jin fled overnight in panic and Mingzhou was restored.
value.literal: the Jin forces fled by night in fear, and Mingzhou was pacified again.

value.zh: 九月，帝以仁恭、進通之入寇也，皆由鎮、定為其囊橐，即以葛從周為上將以伐鎮州，遂攻下臨城，渡滹沱以環其城。
value.en: In the ninth month, blaming Zhen and Ding for supplying Rengong and Jintong, he made Ge Congzhou supreme commander against Zhenzhou, took Lincheng, and crossed the Hutuo to invest the city.
value.literal: In the ninth month, because Rengong's and Jintong's invasions had both drawn on Zhen and Ding as their storehouses, he made Ge Congzhou supreme commander to attack Zhenzhou, captured Lincheng, and crossed the Hutuo to surround the city.

value.zh: 帝親領軍繼至，鎮帥王熔俱，納質請盟，仍獻文繒二十萬以犒戎士，帝許之。
value.en: The Emperor followed in person; Wang Rong of Zhen sent hostages, sued for peace, and offered two hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army—the Emperor agreed.
value.literal: The Emperor personally led the army to follow; the Zhen commander Wang Rong submitted hostages and begged alliance, and also presented two hundred thousand bolts of figured silk to reward the troops; the Emperor consented.

value.zh: 十月，晉人以帝宿兵于趙，遂南下太行，急攻河陽，留後侯言與都將閻寶力戰固守，僅而獲全。
value.en: In the tenth month, with the Emperor camped in Zhao, the Jin rushed south through the Taihang and hammered Heyang; Hou Yan and Yan Bao held on by sheer force and barely kept the city.
value.literal: In the tenth month the Jin, because the Emperor was encamped in Zhao, marched south through the Taihang in haste and attacked Heyang urgently; the acting governor Hou Yan and Commander Yan Bao fought stubbornly to hold firm and barely survived intact.

value.zh: 十一月，以張存敬為上將，自甘陵發軍，北侵幽、薊，連拔瀛、莫二郡，遂移軍以攻中山。
value.en: In the eleventh month Zhang Cunjing marched from Ganling north into You and Ji, took Ying and Mo in turn, then turned on Zhongshan.
value.literal: In the eleventh month he made Zhang Cunjing supreme commander, launched the army from Ganling, invaded You and Ji to the north, captured Ying and Mo in succession, and then shifted the army to attack Zhongshan.

value.zh: 定帥王郜以精甲二萬戰於懷德亭，盡殪之。
value.en: Ding's Wang Gao met him at Huaide Pavilion with twenty thousand elite armored troops and was annihilated.
value.literal: The Ding commander Wang Gao fought with twenty thousand picked armored troops at Huaide Pavilion; they were utterly destroyed.

value.zh: 郜懼，奔於太原。
value.en: Gao fled in terror to Taiyuan.
value.literal: Gao in fear fled to Taiyuan.

value.zh: 遲明，大軍集於城下，郜季父處直持印鑰乞降，亦以繒帛三十萬為獻，帝即以處直代郜領其鎮焉。
value.en: By dawn the army stood before the walls; Gao's uncle Wang Chuzhi came out with seal and keys to surrender and gave three hundred thousand bolts of silk—the Emperor installed Chuzhi in Gao's place.
value.literal: At daybreak the great army gathered below the city; Gao's uncle by descent Chuzhi held out the seal and keys to beg surrender, and also presented three hundred thousand bolts of silk as tribute; the Emperor at once had Chuzhi replace Gao in command of the circuit.

value.zh: 是月，燕人劉守光赴援中山，寨于易水之上，繼為康懷英、張存敬等所敗，斬獲甚眾。
value.en: That month Liu Shouguang of Yan marched to save Zhongshan and camped on the Yishui; Kang Huaiying and Zhang Cunjing broke him with heavy slaughter.
value.literal: That month the Yan man Liu Shouguang came to relieve Zhongshan and encamped above the Yishui; he was thereafter defeated by Kang Huaiying, Zhang Cunjing, and others, and very many were killed or captured.

value.zh: 由是河朔知懼，皆弭伏焉。
value.en: Thereafter all Hebei submitted in fear.
value.literal: From this the Hebei region knew fear and all submitted.

value.zh: 光化元年正月，帝遣葛從周統諸將略地于山東，遂次於邢、洺。
value.en: In the first month of Guanghua 1 the Emperor sent Ge Congzhou to lead the generals in raiding Shandong, and they halted at Xing and Ming.
value.literal: In the first month of the first year of Guanghua, the Emperor sent Ge Congzhou to command the generals in raiding Shandong, and they then halted at Xing and Ming.

value.zh: 三月，昭宗以帝兼領天平軍節度使，余如故。
value.en: In the third month Zhaozong made the Emperor concurrent military governor of the Tianping army; his other posts were unchanged.
value.literal: In the third month Zhaozong had the Emperor additionally hold the post of military governor of the Tianping Army; the rest remained as before.

value.zh: 四月，滄州節度使盧廷彥為燕軍所攻，棄城奔于魏，魏人送於汴。
value.en: In the fourth month Lu Tingyan of Cangzhou, attacked by the Yan army, abandoned his city and fled to Wei, and the Wei garrison sent him on to Bian.
value.literal: In the fourth month Lu Tingyan, military governor of Cangzhou, was attacked by the Yan army, abandoned the city and fled to Wei; the people of Wei sent him on to Bian.

value.zh: 是月，帝以大軍至钜鹿，屯於城下，敗晉軍萬餘眾于青山口，俘馬千餘匹。
value.en: That month the Emperor marched to Julu, camped beneath the walls, and at Qingshan Pass routed more than ten thousand Jin troops and seized a thousand horses.
value.literal: That month the Emperor with a great army reached Julu, encamped below the city, and at Qingshan Pass defeated more than ten thousand Jin troops, capturing more than a thousand horses.

value.zh: 丁卯，遣從周分兵攻洺州，斬刺史邢善益，擒將五十餘人。
value.en: On dingmao he sent Congzhou to storm Mingzhou, killed Prefect Xing Shanyi, and took more than fifty officers.
value.literal: On dingmao he sent Congzhou with a detachment to attack Ming Prefecture, beheaded Prefect Xing Shanyi, and captured more than fifty officers.

value.zh: 五月己巳，邢州刺史馬師素棄城遁去。
value.en: On jisi in the fifth month Xingzhou Prefect Ma Shisu abandoned the city and fled.
value.literal: On jisi in the fifth month Ma Shisu, prefect of Xing Prefecture, abandoned the city and fled.

value.zh: 辛未，磁州刺史袁奉滔自剄而死。
value.en: On xinwei Cizhou Prefect Yuan Fengtao killed himself by cutting his throat.
value.literal: On xinwei Yuan Fengtao, prefect of Ci Prefecture, cut his own throat and died.

value.zh: 五日之內，連下三州。
value.en: Within five days three prefectures fell in succession.
value.literal: Within five days three prefectures fell in succession.

value.zh: 因以葛從周兼邢州昭義軍節度使留後，帝遂班師。
value.en: Ge Congzhou was made acting governor of Xingzhou and the Zhaoyi army, and the Emperor withdrew.
value.literal: Thereupon Ge Congzhou was made acting military governor of Xing Prefecture and the Zhaoyi Army, and the Emperor then withdrew the army.

value.zh: 是時，襄州節度使趙匡凝聞帝軍有清口之敗，密附於淮夷。
value.en: Zhao Kuangning of Xiangzhou, hearing of the Emperor's defeat at Qingkou, secretly sided with the Huai rebels.
value.literal: At this time Zhao Kuangning, military governor of Xiang Prefecture, hearing that the Emperor's army had suffered the defeat at Qingkou, secretly attached himself to the Huai barbarians.

value.zh: 七月，帝遣氏叔琮率師伐之。
value.en: In the seventh month the Emperor sent Shi Shuzong against him.
value.literal: In the seventh month the Emperor sent Shi Shuzong to lead troops to attack him.

value.zh: 未幾，泌州刺史趙璠越墉來降；
value.en: Soon Bi Prefect Zhao Fan climbed the wall to surrender;
value.literal: Before long Zhao Fan, prefect of Bi Prefecture, scaled the wall to come surrender;

value.zh: 隨州刺史趙匡琳臨陣就擒。
value.en: and Suizhou Prefect Zhao Kuanglin was taken in battle.
value.literal: Zhao Kuanglin, prefect of Sui Prefecture, was captured on the spot in battle.

value.zh: 八月，赫連鐸誘幽州李匡威之眾八萬，寇天成軍，遂攻雲州，營於州北，連亙數里。
value.en: In the eighth month Helian Duo won over eighty thousand of Li Kuangwei's Youzhou troops, struck Tiancheng Army, then besieged Yunzhou with camps stretching several li north of the city.
value.literal: Eighth month, Helian Duo induced eighty thousand of Youzhou Li Kuangwei's troops, raided Tiancheng Army, then attacked Yunzhou, encamping north of the prefecture in a line several li long.

value.zh: 武皇潛軍入於雲州，詰旦，出騎軍以擊之，斬獲數萬，李匡威燒營而遁。
value.en: Wuhuang slipped into Yunzhou with his army; at dawn his horsemen fell on them, killing or capturing tens of thousands, and Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.
value.literal: Wuhuang secretly entered Yunzhou with troops; at dawn he led cavalry out to attack, beheading and capturing tens of thousands; Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.

value.zh: 十月，邢州李存孝叛，納款於梁，李存信構之也。
value.en: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao of Xingzhou rebelled and went over to Liang after Li Cunxin set him up.
value.literal: Tenth month, Xingzhou's Li Cunxiao rebelled, submitted allegiance to Liang; Li Cunxin had framed him.

value.zh: 景福二年春，大舉以伐王鎔，以其通好於李存孝也。
value.en: In the spring of Jingfu 2 Wuhuang marched in force against Wang Rong for keeping ties with Li Cunxiao.
value.literal: Spring of Jingfu year 2, a great campaign was launched against Wang Rong because he was on good terms with Li Cunxiao.

value.zh: 二月，攻天長鎮，旬日不下。
value.en: In the second month he attacked Tianchang Fort, which held out for ten days.
value.literal: Second month, they attacked Tianchang Fort; for ten days it would not fall.

value.zh: 王鎔出師三萬來援，武皇逆戰於叱日嶺下，鎮人敗，斬首萬餘級。
value.en: Wang Rong sent thirty thousand reinforcements; Wuhuang met them at Chiri Ridge, routed the Zhen army, and took more than ten thousand heads.
value.literal: Wang Rong sent thirty thousand men to the relief; Wuhuang met them below Chiri Ridge; the Zhen men were defeated and more than ten thousand heads were taken.

value.zh: 時歲饑，軍乏食，脯屍肉而食之。
value.en: Famine left the army starving; they ate dried flesh from the dead.
value.literal: Famine struck that year; the army lacked food and dried flesh from corpses to eat.

value.zh: 進軍下井陘，李存孝將兵夜入鎮州，鎮人乞師於汴；
value.en: He pushed down Jingxing Pass; Li Cunxiao stole into Zhenzhou by night while the city called on Bian for aid;
value.literal: Advancing through Jingxing Pass, Li Cunxiao led troops by night into Zhenzhou; the Zhen men begged Bian for troops;

value.zh: 汴帥方攻時溥，不暇應之。
value.en: but the Bian commander was busy attacking Shi Pu and could not answer.
value.literal: The Bian commander was then attacking Shi Pu and had no leisure to respond.

value.zh: 乃求援於幽州，李匡威率兵赴之，武皇乃班師。
value.en: Wang Rong turned to Youzhou; Li Kuangwei marched to help, and Wuhuang withdrew.
value.literal: They then sought aid from Youzhou; Li Kuangwei led troops to the rescue, and Wuhuang withdrew the army.

value.zh: 七月，武皇討李存孝於邢州，遂攻平山，渡滹水，攻鎮州。
value.en: In the seventh month Wuhuang attacked Li Cunxiao at Xingzhou, took Pingshan, crossed the Hutuo, and moved on Zhenzhou.
value.literal: Seventh month, Wuhuang campaigned against Li Cunxiao at Xingzhou, then attacked Pingshan, crossed the Hutuo River, and attacked Zhenzhou.

value.zh: 王鎔懼，以帛五十萬犒軍，請修舊好，仍以鎮、冀之師助擊存孝，許之。
value.en: Wang Rong, in terror, sent five hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward the army, sued for peace, and pledged Zhen and Ji troops against Cunxiao; Wuhuang agreed.
value.literal: Wang Rong was afraid; with five hundred thousand bolts of silk he rewarded the army, asked to renew the old friendship, and still offered Zhen and Ji troops to help strike Cunxiao; this was granted.

value.zh: 武皇進圍邢州。
value.en: Wuhuang pressed the siege of Xingzhou.
value.literal: Wuhuang advanced to besiege Xingzhou.

value.zh: 十二月，武皇狩於近郊，獲白兔，有角長三寸。
value.en: In the twelfth month he hunted near the capital and took a white hare with three-inch horns.
value.literal: Twelfth month, Wuhuang hunted near the suburbs and caught a white hare with horns three inches long.

value.zh: 景福元年正月，鎮州王鎔恃燕人之援，率兵十餘萬攻邢州之堯山。
value.en: In the first month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, backed by the Yan, marched more than one hundred thousand men against Yaoshan in Xingzhou.
value.literal: First month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, relying on Yan aid, led more than one hundred thousand men to attack Yaoshan in Xingzhou.

value.zh: 武皇遣李存信將兵應援，李存孝素與存信不協，遞相猜貳，留兵不進。
value.en: Wuhuang sent Li Cunxin to relieve the siege, but Li Cunxiao, long at odds with Cunxin, each suspecting the other, kept his troops from advancing.
value.literal: Wuhuang sent Li Cunxin with troops to relieve the siege; Li Cunxiao had long been at odds with Cunxin, each suspecting the other, and held his men back.

value.zh: 武皇又遣李嗣勳、李存審將兵援之，大破燕、趙之眾，斬首三萬，收其軍實。
value.en: Wuhuang then sent Li Sixun and Li Cunshen to reinforce them, routed the Yan and Zhao armies, took thirty thousand heads, and captured their stores.
value.literal: Wuhuang also sent Li Sixin and Li Cunshen with troops to reinforce them, thoroughly defeated the Yan and Zhao forces, beheaded thirty thousand, and seized their military stores.

value.zh: 三月，武皇進軍渡滹沱，攻欒城，下鼓城、槁城。
value.en: In the third month he advanced across the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.
value.literal: Third month, Wuhuang advanced, crossed the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.

value.zh: 四月，燕軍寇雲、代，武皇班師。
value.en: In the fourth month Yan forces raided Yun and Dai, and Wuhuang withdrew.
value.literal: Fourth month, Yan troops raided Yun and Dai; Wuhuang withdrew the army.

value.zh: 周德威，字鎮遠，小字陽五，朔州馬邑人也。
value.en: Zhou Dewei, whose courtesy name was Zhenyuan and childhood name Yangwu, was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.
value.literal: Zhou Dewei, courtesy name Zhenyuan, childhood name Yangwu, was a native of Mayi in Shuozhou.

value.zh: 初事武皇為帳中騎督，驍勇，便騎射，膽氣智數皆過人。
value.en: He first served Emperor Wu as captain of the guard cavalry. Fierce in battle and expert at mounted archery, he surpassed other men in courage, resolve, and cunning.
value.literal: At first he served Emperor Wu as captain of the guard cavalry; he was fierce and brave, skilled at mounted archery, and in daring, spirit, and stratagem he surpassed other men.

value.zh: 久在雲中，諳熟邊事，望煙塵之警，懸知兵勢。
value.en: After long service at Yunzhong he knew the frontier inside out; from the dust of distant alarms he could read the enemy's movements at a glance.
value.literal: Long stationed at Yunzhong, he was thoroughly versed in frontier affairs; at the sight of dust and smoke warnings he could foresee military dispositions.

value.zh: 乾寧中，為鐵林軍使，武皇討王行瑜，以功加檢校左僕射，移內衙軍副。
value.en: During the Qianning reign he was made commissioner of the Iron Forest Army. When Emperor Wu campaigned against Wang Xingyu, Dewei was promoted for merit to acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and transferred to deputy commander of the inner guard.
value.literal: During the Qianning era he became commissioner of the Iron Forest Army; when Emperor Wu campaigned against Wang Xingyu, for merit he was given the additional title of acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and transferred to deputy commander of the inner guard.

value.zh: 七年，岐人攻靈夏，遣使來求助，德威渡河以應之；
value.en: In the seventh year the Qi attacked Ling and Xia and sent envoys asking for aid. Dewei crossed the Yellow River to answer them.
value.literal: In the seventh year the Qi people attacked Ling and Xia; they sent envoys to ask aid, and Dewei crossed the river to respond.

value.zh: 師還，授蕃漢馬步總管。
value.en: When the army returned he was appointed overall commander of tribal and Han horse and foot.
value.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed overall commander of tribal and Han horse and foot.

value.zh: 七年十一月，汴人據深、冀，汴將王景仁軍八萬次柏鄉，鎮州節度使王鎔來告難，帝遣德威率前軍出井陘，屯於趙州。
value.en: In the eleventh month of the seventh year the Bian held Shen and Ji. The Bian general Wang Jingren camped at Baixiang with eighty thousand men. Wang Rong, military commissioner of Zhenzhou, sent word that he was in peril. The emperor sent Dewei with the vanguard through Jingxing Pass to encamp at Zhaozhou.
value.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year the Bian held Shen and Ji; the Bian general Wang Jingren with eighty thousand troops halted at Baixiang. Wang Rong, military commissioner of Zhenzhou, came to report distress; the emperor sent Dewei to lead the vanguard out through Jingxing Pass and encamp at Zhaozhou.

value.zh: 十二月，帝親征。
value.en: In the twelfth month the emperor took the field in person.
value.literal: In the twelfth month the emperor personally campaigned.

value.zh: 二十五日，進薄汴營，距柏鄉五里，營於野河上。
value.en: On the twenty-fifth they pressed close to the Bian camp, five li from Baixiang, and pitched their tents on the Ye River.
value.literal: On the twenty-fifth day they advanced close to the Bian camp, five li from Baixiang, and encamped on the Ye River.

value.zh: 汴將韓率精兵三萬，鎧甲皆被繒綺，金銀炫曜，望之森然，我軍懼形於色。
value.en: The Bian general Han led thirty thousand elite troops in armor draped with brocade, gold and silver glittering so that they looked terrifying from afar. Fear showed plainly on our men's faces.
value.literal: The Bian general Han led thirty thousand elite troops; their armor was all draped in silk brocade, gold and silver dazzling, and seen from afar they looked grim; our army's fear showed on their faces.

value.zh: 德威謂李存璋曰：「賊結陣而來，觀其形勢，誌不在戰，欲以兵甲耀威耳。
value.en: Dewei told Li Cunzhang, "The enemy advances in battle order, but their intent is not to fight. They mean only to dazzle us with arms and armor.
value.literal: Dewei said to Li Cunzhang, "The foe comes in formed array; judging their posture, their intent is not battle—they wish only to dazzle with arms and armor.

value.zh: 我軍人乍見其來，謂其鋒不可當，此時不挫其銳，吾軍不振矣！」
value.en: Our men, seeing them for the first time, think their charge cannot be stopped. If we do not blunt their pride now, our army will never recover its spirit!"
value.literal: Our men, seeing them come all at once, say their edge cannot be withstood; if at this moment we do not blunt their keenness, our army will not be roused!"

value.zh: 乃遣存璋諭諸軍曰：「爾見此賊軍否？
value.en: He sent Cunzhang to rally the troops and asked, "Do you see this enemy host?
value.literal: He then sent Cunzhang to instruct the armies, saying, "Do you see this bandit host?

value.zh: 是汴州天武健兒，皆屠沽傭販，虛有表耳，縱被精甲，十不當一，擒獲足以為資。」
value.en: They are the Heaven Martial guards of Bianzhou—nothing but butchers, peddlers, and hired hands. Their splendor is empty show. Fine armor or not, ten of them are not worth one of us. Capture them and you will profit."
value.literal: They are the Heaven Martial stalwarts of Bianzhou—all butchers, peddlers, and hired sellers; their show is empty. Even if clad in fine armor, ten are not equal to one; capture them and that will be enough for profit."

value.zh: 德威自率精騎擊其兩偏，左馳右決，出沒數四。
value.en: Dewei himself led elite cavalry against both flanks, wheeling left and right and appearing and vanishing again and again.
value.literal: Dewei himself led elite cavalry to strike both their flanks, charging left and breaking right, appearing and vanishing four or five times.

value.zh: 是日，獲賊百餘人，賊渡河而退。
value.en: That day they took more than a hundred prisoners, and the enemy crossed the river and withdrew.
value.literal: That day they took more than a hundred of the foe; the bandits crossed the river and withdrew.

value.zh: 德威謂莊宗曰：「賊驕氣充盛，宜按兵以待其衰。」
value.en: Dewei told Emperor Zhuangzong, "The enemy's pride is at its height. We should hold our ground and wait for it to fade."
value.literal: Dewei said to Emperor Zhuangzong, "The bandits' arrogant spirit is full; we should hold the army and wait for their decline."

value.zh: 莊宗曰：「我提孤軍，救難解紛，三鎮烏合之眾，利在速戰，卿欲持重，吾懼其不可使也。」
value.en: The emperor replied, "I have brought a lone army to rescue allies in distress. These three prefectures' men are a mob gathered in haste; our advantage lies in swift battle. If you insist on caution, I fear the moment will pass us by."
value.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong said, "I have led a lone army to rescue distress and settle strife; the three prefectures' crowd gathered like blackbirds—profit lies in swift battle. You wish to be weighty; I fear that cannot be applied."

value.zh: 德威曰：「 鎮、定之士，長於守城，列陣野戰，素非便習。
value.en: Dewei said, "The men of Zhen and Ding excel at defending walls. Fighting in open field arrays is not their strength.
value.literal: Dewei said, "The men of Zhen and Ding excel at defending cities; to deploy in array for field battle is not their accustomed skill.

value.zh: 我師破賊，惟恃騎軍，平田廣野，易為施功。
value.en: To defeat the enemy we depend wholly on cavalry. On level plains and open country we can fight to our advantage.
value.literal: Our army in defeating the bandits relies solely on cavalry; on level fields and broad wilds it is easy to exert force.

value.zh: 今壓賊營，令彼見我虛實，則勝負未可必也。」
value.en: If we press close to their camp and let them see our full strength, victory and defeat become uncertain."
value.literal: Now we press on the bandit camp and let them see our strength and weakness; then victory and defeat cannot be certain."

value.zh: 莊宗不悅，退臥帳中。
value.en: The emperor was displeased and withdrew to his tent to lie down.
value.literal: Emperor Zhuangzong was displeased and withdrew to lie in his tent.

value.zh: 德威患之，謂監軍張承業曰：「王欲速戰，將烏合之徒，欲當劇賊，所謂不量力也。
value.en: Dewei was deeply troubled. He told army supervisor Zhang Chengye, "His Majesty wants a quick battle. He would pit a hastily gathered mob against a formidable foe. That is to misjudge one's strength.
value.literal: Dewei was troubled by this and said to the army supervisor Zhang Chengye, "The king wishes swift battle, will take a mob gathered like blackbirds and meet fierce bandits—what is called not measuring one's strength.

value.zh: 去賊咫尺，限此一渠水，彼若早夜以略彴渡之，吾族其為俘矣。
value.en: We stand a foot from the enemy, with only this ditch between us. If they cross by night on light bridges, our whole army will be taken prisoner.
value.literal: A mere foot from the bandits, with only this ditch between—if they cross by night on light bridges, our clans will be their captives.

value.zh: 若退軍鄗邑，引賊離營，彼出則歸，復以輕騎掠其芻餉，不逾月，敗賊必矣。」
value.en: If we withdraw to Gaoyi and lure them from their camp, we can strike when they advance and fall back when they retreat, then send light cavalry to raid their fodder and supplies. Within a month the enemy will surely be broken."
value.literal: If we withdraw the army to Gaoyi, draw the bandits from camp, when they come out we return, and again with light cavalry raid their fodder and grain, within a month the defeated bandits are certain."

value.zh: 承業入言，莊宗乃釋然。
value.en: Chengye went in and spoke to the emperor, who then accepted the plan with relief.
value.literal: Chengye entered and spoke; Emperor Zhuangzong then was relieved.

value.zh: 德威得降人問之，曰「景仁下令造浮橋數日」，果如德威所料。
value.en: Dewei questioned a prisoner, who said, "Jingren has ordered floating bridges built for several days"—just as Dewei had predicted.
value.literal: Dewei questioned a surrendered man, who said, "Jingren has ordered floating bridges built for several days"—exactly as Dewei had foreseen.

value.zh: 二十七日，乃退軍保鄗邑。
value.en: On the twenty-seventh the army withdrew to Gaoyi.
value.literal: On the twenty-seventh day they then withdrew the army to hold Gaoyi.

value.zh: 李崧，深州饒陽人。
value.en: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.
value.literal: Li Song was a native of Raoyang in Shen Prefecture.

value.zh: 父舜卿，本州錄事參軍。
value.en: His father Shunqing had been recording officer and military adjutant of that prefecture.
value.literal: His father Shunqing served as recording officer and military adjutant of the prefecture.

value.zh: 崧幼而聰敏，十餘歲為文，家人奇之。
value.en: From childhood Song was quick-witted; by his mid-teens he was already writing essays, and his family marveled at him.
value.literal: Song was clever from childhood; in his teens he could compose essays, and his family regarded him as extraordinary.

value.zh: 弱冠，本府署為參軍。
value.en: At twenty he took a post as military adjutant in the local prefectural office.
value.literal: At the age of twenty he was appointed military adjutant in the prefectural office.

value.zh: 其父嘗謂宗人李鏻曰：「大醜生處，形奇氣異，前途應不居徒勞之地，賴吾兄誨激之。」
value.en: His father once told his kinsman Li Lin, "Where Dachou was born, the boy's looks were odd and his spirit unlike others; he is not meant to waste his life in drudgery—it will be up to my elder brother to teach and urge him on."
value.literal: His father once said to his clansman Li Lin: "Where Dachou was born, his form was strange and his spirit unusual; his future should not lie in vain toil—it depends on my elder brother to instruct and spur him."

value.zh: 大醜即崧之小字也。
value.en: Dachou was Song's childhood name.
value.literal: Dachou was Song's childhood name.

value.zh: 同光初，魏王繼岌為興聖宮使，兼領鎮州節鉞，崧以參軍從事。
value.en: Early in the Tongguang reign, Prince of Wei Jiji served as director of the Xingsheng Palace while also holding the military commission of Zhen Prefecture, and Song went with him as adjutant.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Tongguang era, Prince of Wei Jiji was Director of the Xingsheng Palace and concurrently held the military commission of Zhen Prefecture; Song accompanied him as adjutant.

value.zh: 時推官李蕘掌書，崧見其起草不工，密謂掌事呂柔曰：「令公皇子，天下瞻望，至於尺牘往來，章表論列，稍須文理合宜。
value.en: The judicial officer Li Rao then handled correspondence, and Song, finding his drafts clumsy, quietly told the steward Lü Rou, "His Lordship is an imperial prince, the hope of the realm; whatever letters and memorials go out should at least be literate and apt.
value.literal: At the time the judicial officer Li Rao managed documents; Song saw that his drafting was unskilled and secretly told the steward Lü Rou: "His Lordship is an imperial prince, watched by all under Heaven; as for letters exchanged and memorials submitted, the prose ought at least to be literate and fitting.

value.zh: 李侍御起草，未能盡善。」
value.en: Censor Li's drafts are not quite up to the mark."
value.literal: Censor Li's drafts are not fully adequate."

value.zh: 呂曰：「公試代為之。」
value.en: Lü replied, "Why don't you try drafting them yourself?"
value.literal: Lü said: "Sir, try drafting them yourself."

value.zh: 呂得崧所作，示盧質、馮道，皆稱之。
value.en: Lü took what Song had written and showed it to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao, and both praised it.
value.literal: Lü obtained what Song had written and showed it to Lu Zhi and Feng Dao; both praised it.

value.zh: 繇是擢為興聖宮巡官，獨掌奏記。
value.en: On that account he was promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and given sole charge of memorials and reports.
value.literal: Thereupon he was promoted to touring officer of the Xingsheng Palace and alone managed memorials and reports.

value.zh: 莊宗入洛，授太常寺協律郎。
value.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Song was made harmonizing officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
value.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Song was appointed harmonizing officer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

value.zh: 王師伐蜀，繼岌為都統，以崧掌書記。
value.en: When the imperial forces marched against Shu, Jiji was overall commander and Song served as his chief secretary.
value.literal: When the imperial army campaigned against Shu, Jiji was overall commander and Song served as chief secretary.

value.zh: 蜀平，樞密使郭崇韜為宦官誣構，繼岌遂殺崇韜父子，外尚未知。
value.en: After Shu fell, eunuchs framed Military Affairs Commissioner Guo Chongtao, and Jiji killed Chongtao and his son; the news had not yet spread beyond their camp.
value.literal: After Shu was pacified, the eunuchs slandered the Commissioner of Military Affairs Guo Chongtao, and Jiji thereupon killed Chongtao and his son; those outside still did not know.

value.zh: 崧白繼岌曰：「王何為作此危事？
value.en: Song said to Jiji, "Your Highness, why do this reckless thing?
value.literal: Song told Jiji: "Your Highness, why commit this perilous act?

value.zh: 至於不容崇韜，至洛誅之未晚。
value.en: If Chongtao cannot be tolerated, you could still put him to death after you reach Luoyang.
value.literal: As for not tolerating Chongtao, it would not be too late to execute him after reaching Luoyang.

value.zh: 今懸軍五千里，無咫尺書詔，便殺重臣，非謀也。」
value.en: Your army is five thousand li from home with no word from the throne, yet you have killed a great minister—that is no sound policy."
value.literal: Now the army is isolated five thousand li away, without the slightest imperial edict, yet a great minister is killed—this is not sound planning."

value.zh: 繼岌曰：「吾亦悔之。」
value.en: Jiji said, "I regret it as well."
value.literal: Jiji said: "I too regret it."

value.zh: 崧召書吏三四人，登樓去梯，取黃紙矯寫詔書，倒使都統印發之。
value.en: Song called three or four clerks, had them climb a tower and pull up the ladder, forged an edict on yellow paper, and had it issued with the overall commander's seal impressed upside down.
value.literal: Song summoned three or four clerks, went up a tower and removed the ladder, took yellow paper and forged an edict, and had the overall commander's seal impressed upside down to issue it.

value.zh: 翌日，告諸軍，軍情稍定。
value.en: The next day he announced it to the troops, and army morale gradually settled.
value.literal: The next day he announced it to the armies, and morale gradually steadied.

value.zh: 及自蜀還，明宗革命，任圜以宰相判三司，用崧為鹽鐵推官，賜緋。
value.en: After the return from Shu, Emperor Mingzong took the throne; Ren Huan, serving as chancellor in charge of the Three Departments, appointed Song salt-and-iron investigating officer and gave him crimson robes.
value.literal: When he returned from Shu, Emperor Mingzong seized power; Ren Huan, as chancellor overseeing the Three Departments, employed Song as salt and iron investigating officer and granted him crimson robes.

value.zh: 丁內艱，歸鄉里。
value.en: When his mother died he went into mourning and returned home.
value.literal: He entered mourning for his mother and returned to his home district.

value.zh: 服闋，鎮帥範延光奏署掌書記。
value.en: After mourning he was appointed chief secretary on Fan Yanguang's recommendation as military governor.
value.literal: When mourning ended, the military governor Fan Yanguang memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.

value.zh: 延光為樞密使，拜拾遺，直樞密院，遷補闕、起居郎、尚書郎，充職如故。
value.en: When Yanguang became military affairs commissioner, Song was made remonstrance official and attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs; he rose through censor, recorder of the ruler's movements, and secretariat posts while keeping his original duties.
value.literal: When Yanguang became Commissioner of Military Affairs, Song was appointed remonstrance official and served in the Bureau of Military Affairs; he was promoted to censor, recorder of the ruler's movements, and secretary in the Secretariat, while continuing in his duties as before.

value.zh: 長興末，改翰林學士。
value.en: Near the end of the Changxing reign he was made a Hanlin academician.
value.literal: At the end of the Changxing era he was made Hanlin academician.

value.zh: 清泰初，拜端明殿學士、戶部侍郎。
value.en: Early in the Qingtai reign he was made Duanming Hall academician and vice minister of revenue.
value.literal: At the beginning of the Qingtai era he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall and vice minister of revenue.

value.zh: 鏻少舉進士，累舉不第。
value.en: Lin took the jinshi examination repeatedly in youth and failed.
value.literal: Lin in youth took the jinshi examination and failed repeatedly.

value.zh: 客遊河朔，稱清海軍掌書記，謁定州王處直，不見禮。
value.en: As a guest in Hebei he styled himself chief secretary of the Qinghai Army and called on Wang Chuzhi of Ding, who slighted him.
value.literal: Traveling as a guest in Hebei, he called himself chief secretary of the Qinghai Army and called on Wang Chuzhi of Ding Prefecture, who did not treat him with courtesy.

value.zh: 鏻即脫綠被緋，入常山謁要人李宏規，以宗姓請兄事之，由是得進。
value.en: He shed his official robes, went to Changshan, called on Li Honggui as a clansman asking to serve him as elder brother, and thereby advanced.
value.literal: Lin then removed his green robe and crimson, entered Changshan, and called on the powerful Li Honggui, asking as a clansman to serve him as elder brother, and thereby advanced.

value.zh: 趙王镕辟為從事，镕卒，復為王德明賓客。
value.en: Wang Rong, Prince of Zhao, made him an aide; after Rong's death he served Wang Deming as guest.
value.literal: Wang Rong, Prince of Zhao, made him an aide; when Rong died, he again became guest of Wang Deming.

value.zh: 德明使鏻聘於唐莊宗，鏻密疏德明之罪，且言可圖之狀，莊宗嘉之。
value.en: Deming sent him on embassy to Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong; Lin secretly reported Deming's crimes and how he could be taken; Zhuangzong praised him.
value.literal: Deming sent Lin on a mission to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang; Lin secretly memorialized Deming's crimes and described how he could be taken; Zhuangzong praised this.

value.zh: 及常山平，以鏻為霸府支使。
value.en: When Changshan fell, Lin was made branch secretary at the hegemonic headquarters.
value.literal: When Changshan was pacified, Lin was made branch secretary of the hegemonic headquarters.

value.zh: 嘗從容請於莊宗曰：「鏻有四子，請誅之。」
value.en: He once casually asked Zhuangzong, "I have four sons—please execute them."
value.literal: He once casually asked Zhuangzong: "Lin has four sons—please execute them."

value.zh: 莊宗問其故，對曰：「此輩生於常山，稟勃亂之氣，不可留也。」
value.en: Zhuangzong asked why; he said, "Born in Changshan, they bear its turbulent spirit—they cannot be kept."
value.literal: Zhuangzong asked the reason; he replied: "These were born in Changshan and bear its turbulent air—they cannot be kept."

value.zh: 莊宗笑而止。
value.en: Zhuangzong laughed and refused.
value.literal: Zhuangzong laughed and stopped it.

value.zh: 同光初，授宗正卿，俄兼工部侍郎。
value.en: Early in Tongguang he was director of the imperial clan court and soon vice minister of works.
value.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was appointed director of the imperial clan court and soon also vice minister of works.

value.zh: 常山有唐啟運陵，鏻受富民李守恭賂，署為陵臺令，守恭暴橫，為長吏所訴，按之以聞，鏻左授司農少卿，削金紫，未幾，出為河府副使。
value.en: Changshan holds the Tang Qiyun tomb; Lin took a bribe from Li Shougong and made him tomb magistrate; Shougong's violence was reported; Lin was demoted to vice minister of agriculture, stripped of gold and purple, then sent out as He prefecture deputy commissioner.
value.literal: Changshan has the Tang Qiyun tomb; Lin took a bribe from the wealthy Li Shougong and appointed him tomb platform magistrate; Shougong was violent and was reported by the chief official; investigated and reported up, Lin was demoted to vice minister of agriculture and stripped of gold and purple; before long he went out as deputy commissioner of the He prefecture.

value.zh: 明宗即位，歷兵部、戶部侍郎，工部、戶部尚書。
value.en: Under Mingzong he served as vice ministers of war and revenue and as ministers of works and revenue.
value.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Lin served as vice minister of war, vice minister of revenue, minister of works, and minister of revenue.

value.zh: 長興中，以與明宗有舊，常貯入相之意，從容謂時相曰：「唐祚中興，宜敦敘宗室，才高者合居相位。
value.en: In Changxing, with old ties to Mingzong, he often hoped for the chancellorship and told the chancellors, "The Tang restoration should honor the clan; the able should hold the highest office.
value.literal: In Changxing, because of old ties with Mingzong, he often harbored intent to enter the chancellorship and casually told the chancellors: "The Tang restoration should honor the imperial clan; the talented ought to hold the highest office.

value.zh: 仆雖不才，曾事莊宗霸府，見今上於藩邸時。
value.en: Though I lack talent, I served Zhuangzong's headquarters and knew the present emperor in his princely days.
value.literal: Though I am without talent, I once served Zhuangzong's hegemonic headquarters and saw the present emperor in his princely residence.
